Most momentum traders use the wrong 6 months. 📊

The textbook Jegadeesh-Titman trade ranks stocks on the past 6 to 12 months and goes long winners, short losers. Standard. Replicated for 30 years.

Novy-Marx (Journal of Financial Economics, 2012) ripped it apart.

He decomposed the formation window and found something unsettling: the recent 6 months (months 1 to 6) carry almost no predictive power. The entire momentum premium comes from the intermediate window, months 7 to 12.

The complete logic:

🔹 LOOKBACK. Use months 12 through 7 for the formation window. Skip the most recent 6 months entirely.
🔹 RANK stocks by that intermediate return.
🔹 LONG winners, SHORT losers. Equal-weighted.
🔹 HOLD 6 months, Jegadeesh-Titman overlapping-portfolio style.
🔹 Replicated across commodities and international indices.

Gap between intermediate and recent sleeves: up to ~50 bps per month.

Why it matters: simple underreaction stories about price discovery can't explain this. The information embedded in 6-month-old prices outperforms what's in last month's prices. That contradicts every intuitive model retail uses.

For large liquid stocks (where microstructure noise is minimal), the pattern is even sharper.
